candidate: Harness-run duplicate and split-overlap check (new expctl subcommand, standard library only)
what: One pass over each declared split: record count, exact-duplicate groups after a declared normalisation, a repeat-count histogram, exact overlap counts between every pair of splits and, if the user declares a group key, group overlap. Harness code reads sealed splits itself and prints counts only; it never edits data.
problem_here: validity.md section 2 advises these checks but nothing runs them; expctl hash skips data and datasets directories and large files; the agent may not read the sealed test split, so it cannot do the cross-split check itself.
mechanism: hashlib digest of each normalised record; dict of digest to count per split; set intersection across splits; a small JSON of counts keyed to the data fingerprint.
evidence: Train-test overlap affects more than 4% of the validation set of the standard language-model datasets studied (https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.06499, ACL 2022, authors). Removing duplicates erased a 16 to 21 point apparent advantage in one re-identification study (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07399 v1, 2026-09-07, authors). Exact repeats at 10% of tokens cost a 344M language model about a third of its compute at the worst repeat count (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24998 v1, 2026-06-23, authors, single runs). Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Standard technique, no product; expctl.py already has sha256 helpers.
cost: Small: one command and one config entry for record format and normalisation. Standard library reads JSONL, CSV and plain text only; Parquet or Arrow needs the project's environment. Memory grows with unique records. Output can reveal test membership if it lists items, so counts only and one run per fingerprint.
simpler_alternative: Keep the prose advice in validity.md and let the agent write ad hoc scripts (current state; cannot touch the sealed split).
reason: Closes the one data-validity gap the agent cannot close itself, with no dependency; the size of the effect is supported by several independent sources.
cheap_local_trial: A 60-line hashlib script over the train and validation JSONL files of a public dataset already on disk, compared with a manual spot check; minutes, CPU only.

candidate: Order-independent dataset fingerprint in every run record
what: Per split: record count, a content hash that does not depend on row or shard order, the normalisation string and the hash of the build or filter configuration; stored with each run and compared with the baseline's.
problem_here: Runs are comparable only on identical data; the kit's provenance hash covers source files, not data, and the data manifest in validity.md is advice only.
mechanism: Hash of the sorted list of per-record sha256 digests (or their sum modulo 2^256; not XOR, which cancels duplicate records) plus per-file sha256; same idea as the build manifest in shuddhi (corpus hash, filter-config hash, filtered-build hash, per-shard hashes, checkable offline).
evidence: https://github.com/agentanywhere/shuddhi README (v1.3.0, checked 2026-11-11): manifest design and the maintainer's own run on 33M documents. Design argument; no measured effect on results.
maturity: Plain hashing. shuddhi itself is young (52 commits, 2 stars, Apache-2.0, not on PyPI).
cost: Small; hashing large data takes time (cache by path, size and modification time and say so); must be computed by harness code for sealed splits.
simpler_alternative: Sorted list of per-file sha256 values; breaks when shards are rewritten with the same content.
reason: Makes 'same data' checkable in the keep rule of the unattended loop at no dependency cost.
cheap_local_trial: Hash a JSONL split twice, once with rows shuffled; the fingerprints must match. Minutes.

candidate: Budget-matched random-drop control for data-filter hypotheses (reduced form of Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition, arXiv 2610.19343 v1)
what: A filtering or selection step is kept only if it beats a random subset of the same size drawn with the same per-source proportions, by more than the measured noise floor.
problem_here: The planned unattended loop will try data filters; comparing filtered data with all data or with an unmatched random subset confounds better items with less data and with a changed source mix.
mechanism: Extra arms at equal training budget: a same-size random subset and a same-size random subset with the filter's per-source counts. If a source has no eligible items the matched arm cannot be built and the loop reports that instead of a win.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19343 v1 (2026-10-14, CC BY 4.0, authors): only within-source selection exceeded its null band (+29.7 holdout items with 30 of 30 replicates positive; +5.6, marginal, on a second pair; +27.3 with 9 of 9 for a second gate family); redistribution unresolved. No code. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint, four weeks old, retrieval tasks only; control arms as such are long-standing practice.
cost: One or two extra training runs per filter hypothesis; needs a source or group column; small code in the loop controller.
simpler_alternative: Same-size random subset without source matching.
reason: Cheap validity rule that stops the loop from keeping filters whose gain comes from the source mix or the size.
cheap_local_trial: On a small text-classification fine-tune, compare a length filter with a same-size random subset over 3 seeds; under an hour on one GPU.

candidate: No-added-data baseline arm, with judge and quality scores as diagnostics only, for synthetic-data hypotheses
what: Generated or agent-collected training data is accepted only on the frozen evaluator against the same run without it; LLM-judge and quality-rater scores are logged but never decide.
problem_here: Goal 5 and the unattended loop invite synthetic data; an agent will otherwise accept data on its own quality score.
mechanism: Loop keep rule: candidate run (base data plus generated data) against baseline run (base data), equal budget, noise floor applied.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20465 v1 (page date 2026-05-19, CC BY 4.0, authors): several LLM and agent data-construction methods fell below the baseline that adds nothing (Llama-3.1-8B Science 13.2 to 3.1-7.5; General 67.1 to 51.1; Qwen2.5-7B Finance 57.8 to 44.4), best gains about +20; quality-rater metrics correlated at about 0.05-0.09 with downstream results on General. Seeds not stated in the part read. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One benchmark paper with code (no licence file); direction agrees with older model-collapse work (https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17493 v3).
cost: One baseline run the kit requires anyway; no code beyond the keep rule.
simpler_alternative: none
reason: Direct measured evidence that LLM-built data can lower results and that quality scores do not reveal it.
cheap_local_trial: none needed beyond the baseline the kit already mandates

candidate: Frozen data-gate settings and evaluation-isolated generation in unattended mode
what: Generator, solver and judge prompts, filter thresholds and acceptance code sit under frozen_paths; generation commands cannot read evaluation or sealed paths; every generated row carries an origin tag.
problem_here: In unattended mode the agent both produces data and benefits from its acceptance; the guard protects the evaluator and the test set but not a data gate.
mechanism: Existing frozen_paths and sealed_paths in .claude/nn-training.json extended to data-gate files; origin column checked by the data check.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25996 v3 (2026-07-04, authors): data agents tried to pass the weak-strong gate by rewriting the weak solver's prompt to make it weak; hacking and insufficient safeguards listed as limitations. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12413 v2 (2026-11-07, authors): semantic duplicates of test items raise held-out accuracy by 10 to 22 points and pass standard decontamination. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Uses mechanisms the kit already ships.
cost: Config and documentation; the guard is a seatbelt, not a sandbox, so a determined agent can still route around it.
simpler_alternative: An instruction in the skill text (the kit's own validity.md says instructions do little against metric gaming).
reason: A reported, concrete gaming path that the current guard does not cover.
cheap_local_trial: Add a judge prompt file to frozen_paths in a test repository and confirm the guard blocks an edit; minutes.

candidate: Report-only data checks (checks emit counts and review lists, never delete or rewrite data)
what: Every data check writes evidence; removing items is a separate change that the user approves or the loop tests.
problem_here: A duplicate or label check that deletes rows changes the experiment silently and can remove minority data.
mechanism: Checks are read-only commands; removal proposals become journal hypotheses tested with the matched control arm.
evidence: Document-level MinHash removal scored below no deduplication (51.51 against 51.89; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03089 v1, 2026-08-04, authors, single runs). The repetition study warns against filtering repetitive-looking minority data (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24998 v1). In a label-cleaning study about a quarter of general LLM-label disagreements went against the LLM (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22382 v1). A robotics data SDK states the same principle (https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/hflow). Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Principle; no product.
cost: None beyond discipline.
simpler_alternative: none
reason: Three independent sources show that automatic removal can hurt or be wrong.

candidate: Semantic-duplicate blind-spot statement in the validity reference and the final report
what: validity.md and the report template say that exact and n-gram overlap checks do not detect paraphrased copies of evaluation items, name the optional embedding screen, and record which overlap level was checked with which tool version.
problem_here: validity.md section 2 presents n-gram or exact-match checks as the contamination check; the upgrade adds scouting and data generation, which can carry evaluation content into training data in paraphrased form.
mechanism: Two sentences in the reference and one line in the report.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12413 v2 (2026-11-07, authors): semantic duplicates of 76% of CodeForces test items and 100% of MBPP items found in one open post-training corpus; fine-tuning on them raised held-out accuracy by up to 22 points (10 to 11 at realistic rates); gains did not transfer to related benchmarks. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint (second version), consistent with earlier contamination literature.
cost: Text only.
simpler_alternative: none
reason: Costs nothing and keeps reported numbers honest about what was checked.

what: MinHash sketches and LSH-based near-duplicate detection for text; deduplicator objects return keep flags.
problem_here: Near-duplicate counting for text sets too large for a pure-Python loop; optional companion to the core exact check.
mechanism: Several MinHash variants and a sampling pipeline; banded LSH; Jaccard threshold (0.8 in examples), 128 permutations.
evidence: https://github.com/beowolx/rensa README (checked 2026-11-11): 608 times Datasketch and 12 times FastSketch on 7 datasets, maintainer's own benchmark, not replicated; nothing on downstream effect. Wheels including win_amd64 seen at https://pypi.org/pypi/rensa/0.5.0/json.
maturity: First PyPI upload 2024-06-23; 0.5.0 uploaded 2026-09-06; MIT; no runtime dependencies; Python >= 3.8; 317 stars (weak signal); looks like one maintainer.
cost: A binary package; 0.5.0 rejects sketches from older versions, so results are tied to the pinned version; LSH misses some pairs; no semantic matching; the threshold changes counts.
simpler_alternative: datasketch 2.0.0 (Python plus NumPy), or a 40-line standard-library MinHash for sets under about 100k records.
reason: No dependencies, Windows wheels and speed; evidence is self-reported and it needs a pinned version stamp.
cheap_local_trial: pip install rensa==0.5.0 in a scratch venv on Windows or WSL2; deduplicate 100k lines of a public text set at threshold 0.8 and compare the count with exact-hash duplicates; minutes, CPU only.

what: MinHash, LSH and related sketches; the implementation most pipelines compare with.
problem_here: Same as rensa: optional near-duplicate counting.
mechanism: MinHash permutations and banded LSH; 2.0.0 changed the default permutation scheme and offers a 64-bit one.
evidence: https://github.com/ekzhu/datasketch/releases (checked 2026-11-11; release dated 5 Jul, year not shown, 2026 inferred): hash values differ from earlier versions, stored sketches and LSH indexes must be rebuilt, a legacy scheme reads old data; the notes claim a bias fix on large sets, half the sketch memory and about 4 times faster updates (maintainer's statement).
maturity: Long-lived project; licence not shown on the page read (MIT from memory, not re-verified).
cost: NumPy dependency (present in any training environment); slower than the Rust option; the scheme change breaks old indexes.
simpler_alternative: Standard-library MinHash for small sets.
reason: Older and more widely used than a young binary package, but slower; choose one of the two after a trial.
cheap_local_trial: The same 100k-line trial as for rensa; compare counts and time.

what: Semantic deduplication, outlier filtering and representative sampling with static embeddings and a nearest-neighbour index; can deduplicate one set against another and reports which records matched, with scores.
problem_here: Paraphrase-level overlap between training or generated data and validation data, which exact and MinHash checks miss.
mechanism: Static embeddings (default model loaded by hub name, so first use downloads it unless cached), approximate or exact index, cosine threshold (0.9 in the README example).
evidence: https://github.com/MinishLab/semhash README and source (checked 2026-11-11): 1.8M text records in about 74 s on CPU, maintainers' benchmark; no downstream measurement. Need shown by https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12413 v2 (semantic duplicates raise held-out accuracy by 10 to 22 points).
maturity: First release 0.1.0 on 2025-01-05; 0.5.0 on 2026-09-30; MIT; Python >= 3.10; 979 stars; PyPI attestations present.
cost: Several packages (model2vec, vicinity, numpy and others) and a model download; threshold-dependent counts; static embeddings miss harder paraphrases; for the sealed split it must run inside harness code and print counts only.
simpler_alternative: Core exact check plus a written limitation; or embeddings from the model being trained with a brute-force cosine search for small sets.
reason: The only light CPU tool found for the semantic-duplicate gap; no independent evidence yet.
cheap_local_trial: pip install semhash in a scratch venv; deduplicate the train split of a public QA set against its validation split; read the top 50 matched pairs by hand to choose a threshold; about 15 minutes, CPU only.

what: Incremental MinHash-LSH deduplication for corpora that keep growing, with removal of a previously added dataset.
problem_here: none found (single-machine fine-tuning data is far below its scale)
mechanism: Tiered on-disk index at 128 bytes per document for 16 bands; sketch library pinned to one exact version; version stamp checked at start.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28622 v1 (page date 2026-07-29, authors): 1B documents in about 1.75 h in one process; 11 times LSHBloom and 35 times Milvus-LSH; in-memory LSH needed about 6.5 KB per document; used on more than 30B documents. https://github.com/Zyphra/puffer README: a sketch-library version mismatch raises no error and silently stops matching, hence the stamp. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Apache-2.0; no releases; 8 stars; one organisation; Python 3.10+; removal needs a C compiler.
cost: Compiler needed; a state directory to manage; overkill below roughly 100M documents.
simpler_alternative: rensa or datasketch in memory.
reason: No problem of that scale here; keep the lesson (stamp the sketch version and refuse on mismatch).

what: GPU-accelerated MinHash-LSH deduplication for distributed clusters.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Partially reusable hash function, GPU kernels, streaming instead of data shuffling.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01046 v4 (authors): up to 158 times a CPU tool and 7.8 times a GPU tool on 30M documents with four GPUs; 1.2T tokens in about 3 h on 32 GPUs. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: https://github.com/mcrl/SEDD: 1 star; needs CUDA 12.4 and MPI; research code.
cost: MPI and multi-GPU set-up; would occupy the one training GPU.
simpler_alternative: CPU MinHash.
reason: Cluster-scale tool; nothing in the kit's use needs it.

candidate: Frequency- and length-aware subdocument deduplication (arXiv 2608.03089 v1)
what: Finds repeated spans inside documents and keeps a number of copies that depends on how often the span occurs and how long it is.
problem_here: none found for fine-tuning-size data; relevant only when pretraining a language model on web-scale text.
mechanism: Retention count T = ceil(1 + (g(C) - 1) * a(L)) with g(C) = C(1 - 1/N)^(C-1) and a(L) = max(0, 1 - L/512).
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03089 v1 (2026-08-04, authors): average of 8 benchmarks 52.90 against 51.89 without deduplication, 51.51 for document-level MinHash, 52.14 keep-one, 52.79 suffix array; single runs, no seeds, cost of the pass not stated. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint; no code.
cost: Suffix-array-scale processing; differences under one point without variance estimates.
simpler_alternative: Exact-duplicate report and no removal.
reason: No code and no fit to the kit's scale; its table is the evidence that near-duplicate removal is not automatically a gain.

what: Finds exact and near-duplicate images, train/validation leakage and COCO annotation defects; hashes nominate pairs and a pixel comparison over 8 orientations decides.
problem_here: Image projects have no mechanical cross-split near-duplicate check in the kit.
mechanism: SHA-256, a difference hash and a DCT perceptual hash over rotations and flips, then a grayscale-thumbnail comparison; exit code 0 or 1.
evidence: https://pypi.org/project/vision-data-doctor/ (checked 2026-11-11): the only result is the author's private dataset (81 byte-identical groups across train and validation); effect Unverified. Need supported by https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10144 v1 (at least 118k duplicate pairs across 1034 public 3D medical datasets, authors).
maturity: Single release 2026-09-18; MIT; Alpha; Python >= 3.10; depends on Pillow only; no publish attestation; sweep repository has 3 stars.
cost: Young single-author package without provenance attestation; verification cost grows fast in large duplicate clusters.
simpler_alternative: Core exact file-hash check, or a 30-line difference hash with Pillow.
reason: Right design (nominate, then verify; exit codes for automation) but one alpha release and no independent evidence.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch venv, run its leakage command on a small public image set with a few copied and flipped files planted in the validation folder; minutes.

what: Ranks likely label errors, outliers, near duplicates and non-IID structure from features and out-of-fold predicted probabilities.
problem_here: validity.md asks the agent to inspect about 50 items by hand; there is no ranked list of suspect labels.
mechanism: Confident learning on predicted probabilities; an issue report per dataset.
evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/cleanlab/json and https://github.com/cleanlab/cleanlab (checked 2026-11-11) for version, licence and dependencies. Effect evidence is the project's own published work, not re-read here. Related: an LLM label audit was backed by radiologists in 74% to 92% of sampled disagreements (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22382 v1).
maturity: First PyPI upload 2018-11-22; 2.9.0 uploaded 2026-01-13 and no later release; licence field Apache 2.0 for 2.9.0; 11.7k stars; project status after January 2026 not checked by me.
cost: Needs out-of-fold predictions (extra training runs or a cheap proxy model); numpy, scikit-learn and pandas; flags include false positives, so review before removal.
simpler_alternative: Rank training items by the current model's loss and review the top 100 by hand.
reason: Mature method, but extra runs eat the budget and there has been no release since January 2026.
cheap_local_trial: Fit a linear probe with 5-fold cross-validation on frozen features of a small labelled set, pass the probabilities to the library and read the top 30 flagged items; under 30 minutes.

what: Several LLMs re-derive each label from the source text; items where the majority disagrees with the stored label go to review.
problem_here: Labels derived automatically from text (reports, logs) can be wrong at scale.
mechanism: Independent prompts to several models; majority vote; human check of a sample of disagreements.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22382 v1 (authors): 96.4% agreement with stored labels, kappa 0.884; radiologists sided with the LLM in 72 of 97 general and 91 of 99 lymphadenopathy disagreements; majority vote best; no downstream training result. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One domain study.
cost: Money per item; data leaves the machine unless local models are used; about a quarter of general flags were wrong.
simpler_alternative: Loss-ranked manual review.
reason: Plausible for text-derived labels, but no evidence of better trained models and it can send data to outside services.
cheap_local_trial: Run two local open models on 200 labelled items and count disagreements with the stored labels; about 20 minutes on the GPU.

candidate: DataPrep-Bench and its Distributional Alignment Score (repository commit 877a2a0, 2026-11-02)
what: Benchmark that scores data-preparation methods by downstream fine-tuning; the score is the negative MMD between embeddings of candidate data and a domain proxy set.
problem_here: A cheap predictor of whether a candidate dataset will help would save runs.
mechanism: 5,000 samples per candidate embedded with an 8B embedding model, RBF kernel; correlation with downstream score.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20465 v1 (authors): Pearson r 0.68 General, 0.86 Math, 0.72 Science for the alignment score; about 0.05-0.09 for quality-rater metrics on General; pools of 8 to 14 candidates; about 306 s per candidate. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: https://github.com/OpenDCAI/Data-Preparation-Bench: 17 commits, 241 stars, no releases, no licence file at the root.
cost: Embedding server with an 8B model, Python 3.12 and a fine-tuning framework; correlations from few points; needs a proxy set disjoint from the test set; no licence.
simpler_alternative: A short fine-tune on a subsample scored by the frozen evaluator.
reason: The finding changes the design; the tool is heavy, unlicensed and its metric rests on small samples.

candidate: Data-construction skill shipped in the DataPrep-Bench repository (commit 877a2a0)
what: Skill file, reference and scripts that guide a coding agent through building a fine-tuning dataset.
problem_here: none found that the evidence supports
mechanism: Prompted procedure for a coding agent.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20465 v1 (authors): +19.1 over the baseline in one cell (Llama-3.1-8B Finance), but 13.2 to 7.5 in Science and 57.8 to 55.5 for Qwen2.5-7B Finance. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: No licence; part of a 17-commit repository.
cost: Third-party instruction text loaded into the agent; no licence; mixed results.
simpler_alternative: The kit's own baseline-first rule.
reason: Unlicensed, and its own benchmark shows it can lower results.

candidate: Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition, full four-arm design (arXiv 2610.19343 v1)
what: Four budget-matched arms crossing gate eligibility with source distribution, with null bands calibrated from replicates.
problem_here: Attributing a filter's effect to selection or to source mix.
mechanism: Replicated arms, null calibration, a scan for budgets at which all arms can be built.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19343 v1 (2026-10-14, authors): 30 replicates per comparison resolved one component; redistribution and interaction stayed unresolved. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint; no code.
cost: Tens of training runs per filter; beyond a single-GPU budget for anything but tiny models.
simpler_alternative: The matched random control (separate candidate).
reason: Correct but expensive; the reduced control gives most of the protection.

what: Agent-built training examples accepted when a strong solver succeeds and a weak solver fails by a set margin, plus an outer optimiser that edits the agent's own prompts and harness.
problem_here: Would supply harder synthetic training data for language-model fine-tuning.
mechanism: Challenger, weak solver, strong solver, judge; thresholds 0.65, 0.5 and a 20-point gap; the outer loop keeps a harness edit only on strict validation improvement.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25996 v3 (2026-07-04, authors, own test sets): a 4B model scored 0.366 untrained, 0.500 with plain self-instruct data, 0.632 with agentic data; 6.59 rounds per accepted item; 233 outer iterations, 126 accepted; agents tried to game the gate. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint from a large lab; no code; an unofficial reimplementation appears in the sweep (not read).
cost: Many LLM calls per kept item (no money figure given); the gate can be gamed; test sets built by the same pipeline.
simpler_alternative: Plain generation plus the no-added-data baseline rule.
reason: No code, high cost, authors' own benchmarks; keep its failure mode as a design input.

candidate: Verbalized Sampling (repository as of 2026-11-08; paper arXiv 2510.01171 v4)
what: Ask the model for several responses with stated probabilities to widen the spread of generated data.
problem_here: Generated data that repeats one pattern.
mechanism: Prompt template; optional Python package and CLI that call a provider API.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01171 v4 (2026-07-15, authors): 1.6 to 2.1 times the diversity of direct prompting in creative writing; no fine-tuning result on the pages read. https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19262 v2: moderate diversity helps downstream, high diversity hurts. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: https://github.com/CHATS-lab/verbalized-sampling: Apache-2.0; 824 stars; no releases; PyPI package exists.
cost: Provider key and money, or a local model; more tokens per sample; diversity is not downstream gain.
simpler_alternative: Vary seeds, personas and source documents in the prompt.
reason: Cheap idea, but no downstream evidence, and the diversity literature says more is not always better.
cheap_local_trial: Use the prompt pattern with a local open model on 100 prompts and compare distinct n-gram and duplicate counts with direct prompting; about 15 minutes on the GPU.

what: Synthetic-data generation toolkit: reusable blocks composed by YAML flows, with skills for coding agents.
problem_here: A maintained, licensed way to generate fine-tuning data if the user opts in.
mechanism: Blocks for prompting, parsing and filtering; flows as YAML; calls go to a configured LLM endpoint.
evidence: https://github.com/Red-Hat-AI-Innovation-Team/sdg_hub (checked 2026-11-11): no measured downstream result on the page. General evidence on generated data is mixed (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20465 v1).
maturity: Apache-2.0; v0.9.4 released 2026-06-09; 170 stars; vendor-backed team; Python 3.10+.
cost: Package tree, an LLM endpoint (account and money, or a local server), third-party skill text; no evidence of benefit.
simpler_alternative: A short script calling a local model, under the baseline rule.
reason: The most mature licensed generator in the sweep; adopt only if a trial shows a gain over the no-added-data baseline.
cheap_local_trial: Not minutes: in a scratch venv under WSL2, point it at a local model server, generate 200 QA pairs from 20 documents and fine-tune a small model with and without them over 3 seeds; a few hours.

candidate: One shared skills folder referenced from per-agent plugin manifests (pattern seen in sdg_hub at commit 31efcbe)
what: Claude Code and Codex plugin manifests both point at the same skills folder; a small Cursor permissions file sits beside them; an llms.txt summarises the repository for agents.
problem_here: Goal 4 (ports to Codex CLI and Cursor) without three copies of the skill text.
mechanism: Two manifest files with the same skills path; Codex install by a marketplace command or a symbolic link into the user's agent-skills folder; a Cursor file with allow and deny lists.
evidence: https://github.com/Red-Hat-AI-Innovation-Team/sdg_hub repository files (checked 2026-11-11). One third-party repository; not checked against vendor documentation (Inferred).
maturity: Seen in one vendor-backed repository.
cost: The symbolic-link variant conflicts with the kit's native-Windows constraint, so an installer must copy; manifests are extra files to keep in step.
simpler_alternative: The installer copies the same files into each agent's folder, with one shell and one PowerShell script.
reason: Promising, but it belongs to the agent-platform facet and needs confirmation from vendor documentation.
cheap_local_trial: Copy the kit's skill folder into a scratch repository with both manifest files and check that each CLI lists the skill; minutes if both CLIs are installed.

what: Builds a knowledge graph from source documents and generates question-answer pairs aimed at the model's knowledge gaps.
problem_here: none found beyond generic synthetic-data generation
mechanism: Graph extraction with an LLM, gap detection, multi-hop QA generation.
evidence: https://github.com/InternScience/GraphGen (checked 2026-11-11; paper arXiv 2505.20416): gains reported by the authors; on one benchmark the baseline was higher.
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 1.2k stars (weak signal).
cost: Many LLM calls; a provider or a local server; graph-extraction errors pass into the data.
simpler_alternative: Plain document-grounded QA generation.
reason: Self-reported evidence only and no specific problem here.

what: Ingestion, cleaning, synthetic generation, quality filtering and export for LLM post-training data, with an append-only provenance record per sample.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Pipeline stages with a per-sample provenance chain.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21631 v1 (authors): describes the library; no downstream results. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: 36 stars in the sweep record; repository not read.
cost: Package tree; no evidence.
simpler_alternative: An origin column per row plus the dataset fingerprint.
reason: No results; the per-sample provenance idea is covered more simply.

what: Corpus-building pipeline with a provenance gate, exact and near deduplication, language id, PII redaction, a contamination screen and a hash-based build manifest; drafts a training-content summary for EU rules.
problem_here: Proof of what a model was trained on; its manifest design answers the kit's missing data fingerprint.
mechanism: Origin class declared per source and refused before the file is opened; order-independent corpus hash, filter-config hash and per-shard sha256 in a manifest file.
evidence: https://github.com/agentanywhere/shuddhi (checked 2026-11-11): maintainer's run on 33,047,370 documents on a 2-vCPU machine (97.71% kept, 0.38% exact duplicates, 0.83% near duplicates, largest cluster 84,275 copies). Self-reported; contamination-screen method not documented.
maturity: Apache-2.0; 52 commits; 2 stars; v1.3.0; not on PyPI; 140 offline tests.
cost: Young single-team tool; lexicon and trigram heuristics can drop valid data; the compliance draft is not legal advice (the tool says so).
simpler_alternative: The core fingerprint candidate.
reason: Good design to borrow; too young to depend on.
cheap_local_trial: none (would require cloning and running the tool)

what: Codex skill with an eight-dimension dataset audit tied to Datasheets for Datasets and the NIST AI RMF.
problem_here: A checklist for the journal's data section.
mechanism: Instruction file plus a web-crawling knowledge updater.
evidence: https://github.com/dungnotnull/ai-dataset-quality-audit-agent-skill (checked 2026-11-11): no measurement of any kind.
maturity: MIT; 1 commit; 4 stars.
cost: Third-party instruction text; its updater feeds web content into the skill (an injection path).
simpler_alternative: Eight checklist lines in the kit's own journal template.
reason: No evidence, one commit, network-fed instructions; only the list of dimensions is worth keeping.

what: Dataset-generation skill for several coding agents with generate, verify, dedup, split-safe export and audit scripts.
problem_here: none found that the evidence supports
mechanism: Skill text plus Python scripts; a shell and a PowerShell installer copy it into each agent's skill folder.
evidence: https://github.com/Bhanunamikaze/AI-Dataset-Generator (checked 2026-11-11): no measurement of data quality or downstream effect.
maturity: MIT; 84 commits; 22 stars; no releases.
cost: README promotes a pipe-to-shell install; a flag allows injection content in datasets; third-party instruction text.
simpler_alternative: none needed
reason: No evidence and an unsafe install path; its two-installer approach (shell and PowerShell, copy not link) is the only reusable idea.

candidate: Held-in and held-out non-regression acceptance gate (Self-Harness, arXiv 2606.09498 v3)
what: A proposed change is kept only if neither the set it was developed on nor a second set regresses and at least one improves, with repeated attempts.
problem_here: Keep rule of the unattended loop (goal 1) and of any later tuning of the kit's own skill text.
mechanism: Two evaluation sets, two attempts per candidate, promotion on no regression plus improvement.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09498 v3 (2026-08-20, authors): pass rates rose on three agent benchmarks for three models (for example 42.2 to 53.9 and 18.0 to 36.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.0); the second set is used in the gate, so final numbers are not independent of it; cost and rejection rate not stated. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Preprint with a one-commit repository without a licence.
cost: A second validation split and doubled evaluations; the second split wears out with use.
simpler_alternative: One validation set with a measured noise floor and one confirmation run on a split used once.
reason: Useful shape, but its held-out set is consumed by the gate; a confirmation split used once is cleaner.

what: A rewriting model, trained with rewards from data influence, rephrases and reformats organic text to make more useful pretraining tokens.
problem_here: none found (pretraining when data runs out)
mechanism: Reinforcement learning of a generator with data-influence rewards.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17849 v2 (authors; COLM 2026): 3.4 to 5.2 times the effective tokens of repetition. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Code at https://github.com/cxcscmu/SynPro; needs 7 to 8 GPUs; no single-GPU recipe.
cost: Multi-GPU; complex.
simpler_alternative: More organic data or fewer epochs.
reason: Out of the kit's compute class.

what: Edits pretraining documents through function calls instead of keeping or dropping them.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: A model emits edit programs that are applied to documents.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08646 v1 (2026-07-09, authors): no numbers in the abstract. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint; no code.
cost: Unknown.
simpler_alternative: Rule-based cleaning.
reason: No code and no numbers read.

what: Uses sparse-autoencoder features of the model to control diversity, difficulty and batching of RL post-training data.
problem_here: none found for the default kit; a possible lever for language-model post-training
mechanism: Feature activations as signals for curriculum and batch composition.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27354 v2 (2026-11-05, authors): +3.1% average accuracy and 42% fewer steps with GRPO on a 1.5B math model. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint.
cost: Needs a trained sparse autoencoder for the base model.
simpler_alternative: Difficulty ordering by base-model loss.
reason: Single self-reported result and a heavy prerequisite.

what: Self-evolving system that builds data-preparation pipelines automatically.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Multi-level evolution of pipeline operators.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07001 v3 (authors): about 10 points average gain on seven benchmarks. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint.
cost: Many LLM calls and training runs.
simpler_alternative: Hand-written cleaning plus the control arm.
reason: Self-reported; another benchmark shows such systems can also lower results.

what: Generates training data aimed at the error categories the current model shows.
problem_here: A principled way to choose what to generate, if synthetic data is used at all.
mechanism: Error analysis on a development set, generation per weakness, retraining.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15964 v1 (authors): +6.2% in-distribution and +7.1% on unseen languages. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint.
cost: Error analysis must use validation data only, or it becomes test leakage; generation cost.
simpler_alternative: Collect more real examples of the failing category.
reason: Fits the kit's diagnose-then-act style, but raises the adaptive-reuse risk on the validation set.

what: Runs data-preparation dataflows on a cluster while keeping parent-child lineage between records.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Lineage-aware operators on a cluster runtime.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18703 v1 (authors). Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Code at https://github.com/OpenDCAI/RayOrch (not read).
cost: Cluster framework.
simpler_alternative: Origin and parent-id columns in the data.
reason: Cluster tool; only the lineage idea is relevant and a column covers it.

what: Quality checks for robot-learning episodes that attach evidence and routing tags.
problem_here: none found (robotics-specific)
mechanism: Check functions over episode data; tags route episodes and nothing is deleted.
evidence: https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/hflow (checked 2026-11-11): no measured training effect on the page.
maturity: Apache-2.0; 308 stars; hosted API on request.
cost: Domain-specific; commercial upsell.
simpler_alternative: The report-only rule (separate candidate).
reason: Wrong domain; its principle is adopted separately.

candidate: Fail-closed detector stacking for personal data (clinical de-identification toolkit, arXiv 2611.12709 v1)
what: Rule-based, NER and local-LLM detectors combined so that any detector's hit redacts; the LLM may not veto the others.
problem_here: Training text with personal data, especially before it goes to a rented GPU or a provider (goal 3).
mechanism: Union of detectors; a failed detector blocks release.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12709 v1 (2026-11-09, authors): asked to verify its own findings, the LLM discarded about a quarter of true identifiers. Abstract-level read. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint, two days old; toolkit not read.
cost: Detectors are language- and domain-specific; false positives remove content.
simpler_alternative: Regular expressions for obvious identifiers plus a user confirmation before data leaves the machine.
reason: Relevant to the remote-GPU goal; the evidence is fresh and from one domain.

candidate: Known-answer audit of an LLM judge before it filters data (practice shown by EditJudge-Bench, arXiv 2611.12524 v1)
what: Before a judge model scores or filters data, measure it on a small set with known correct answers and then freeze its prompt format.
problem_here: Optional synthetic-data and label-audit modules rely on a judge.
mechanism: Planted good and bad items; report the judge's AUROC or accuracy; keep the prompt format frozen afterwards.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12524 v1 (2026-11-09, authors): a widely used judge template reached 69.0% AUROC; prompt formatting moved results by up to 14.1 points. Vision-language judges only. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint; the practice is general.
cost: A small labelled set per task.
simpler_alternative: Use no judge; use the frozen evaluator only.
reason: Needed only if a judge-based module is adopted; then it should be mandatory.
cheap_local_trial: Plant 20 corrupted items among 80 good ones and score the judge with a local model; about 15 minutes.

candidate: Model-based quality classifier for pretraining data selection, adapted across languages (arXiv 2610.11585 v1)
what: Small MLPs on encoder embeddings extend an English quality classifier to other languages.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Embedding plus MLP classifier used as a filter.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11585 v1 (2026-10-08, authors). Abstract-level read. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint.
cost: A classifier is one more gate that can remove minority data.
simpler_alternative: No filtering.
reason: Pretraining-scale concern; any filter needs the control arm anyway.

candidate: Two SFT stages then RL, with a capability-targeted pre-screen of items (axion1_0, repository as of 2026-11-02)
what: Two supervised stages on about 18k curated trajectories, then asynchronous GRPO; items the model solves without the target capability are removed; reference answers are built by program.
problem_here: A filter rule for the fine-tuning reference: drop items the base model already solves without the skill being trained.
mechanism: Base-model pre-screen of items; programmatic references.
evidence: https://github.com/bytedance/axion1_0 (Apache-2.0; paper arXiv 2611.03233; checked 2026-11-11): all results self-reported; SFT took about 90 to 240 GPU-hours on 32 GPUs.
maturity: 37 commits; 68 stars; large vendor.
cost: The recipe is far beyond one GPU; the pre-screen alone is cheap (one inference pass).
simpler_alternative: none
reason: Only the pre-screen idea transfers, and it needs the control arm like any filter.
cheap_local_trial: Run the base model on 500 training questions without the tool or context being trained and count how many it already answers; about 20 minutes on the GPU.

what: Compiles natural-language skills into a graph of reusable state-move-outcome units.
problem_here: none found for the data facet; possible relevance to the size of the kit's skill text.
mechanism: Decomposition and deduplication of skill steps.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12041 v1 (2026-11-09, authors): 232 skills to 95 units, score 0.6379 to 0.7478, 38.38% fewer runtime tokens. Abstract-level read. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint, two days old.
cost: Unknown.
simpler_alternative: Keep the skill short by hand.
reason: Other facet; too new.

candidate: Metadata profile for aggregated datasets (MAP, arXiv 2611.10144 v1)
what: Metadata fields that record which source datasets an item came from, so aggregates can be de-duplicated and traced.
problem_here: Projects that combine several public datasets.
mechanism: Per-item source and derivation fields; published perceptual hashes for lookup.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10144 v1 (2026-11-06, authors): at least 118k duplicate pairs among 565k images from 1034 public datasets. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Proposal in one preprint; domain-specific hash service.
cost: Manual metadata work.
simpler_alternative: A source column per record and source-aware counts in the core check.
reason: Too new and domain-bound; the measured overlap supports the core check.

what: Multi-granularity semantic hashing with LLM adjudication for document deduplication.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Learned binary codes, attention-weighted MinHash, LLM checks on under 1% of pairs.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01601 v1 (2026-07-02, authors): no datasets, baselines or accuracy numbers in the abstract. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: One preprint; no code stated.
cost: Unknown; hash models must be trained.
simpler_alternative: SemHash 0.5.0.
reason: Nothing to run and no numbers.

candidate: Multi-source synthetic data: several generator models instead of one (arXiv 2511.01490 v3)
what: When generating fine-tuning data, mix outputs of different generator models.
problem_here: Narrowing of the output distribution after fine-tuning on one model's outputs.
mechanism: Round-robin over generators; origin tag per row.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01490 v3 (2026-04-28, Findings of ACL 2026, authors): diverse sources reduce distribution collapse; no numbers in the abstract. Background: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17493 v3. Checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Peer-reviewed findings paper; abstract-level read.
cost: More providers or local models; each generator's licence terms apply.
simpler_alternative: Keep real data in the mix and cap the synthetic share.
reason: Low cost if a generation module exists; evidence read at abstract level only.
